core_workflow: Verify isort's documented CLI workflow (single/multiple file sorting, recursive directory sorting, --diff preview, -c check-only verification), the documented Python library API (isort.file), and that packaging metadata's Python version floor matches the README's stated requirement. Each CLI test invokes the installed `isort` console script directly on files created in an isolated case directory and asserts exact resulting file content plus exit code and stdout/stderr signals; the library and metadata tests invoke the Python interpreter directly on a small script within the same isolated directory (no shell).
limitations: CLAIM-002 is verified only via consistency with packaging metadata (T08 confirms Requires-Python is >=3.10.0, matching the README's stated floor); no test actually runs isort under an unsupported (<3.10) Python interpreter to confirm the floor is enforced at runtime, since only one interpreter is available in the harness.

CLAIM-001 (pip install) is only indirectly verified: every test's successful invocation of the installed `isort` script (and successful `import isort` in T07/T08) implies installation succeeded, but no test explicitly runs `pip install isort` itself since the harness performs installation before tests run.

Exact stdout wording for 'Fixing <file>' and diff header formatting is based on documented/typical isort CLI behavior; minor cosmetic wording differences across isort versions are tolerated via substring (contains) matching rather than exact text matching for stdout/stderr.

The original argparse unrecognized-flag test (unclaimed CLI error-handling behavior) was removed: it was not grounded in any documented claim and risked misattributing failures to CLAIM-003 if isort's argument-parsing internals changed while the documented sorting behavior remained intact.
The other declared console script, isort-identify-imports, is intentionally left untested per this plan's scope.

evidence: isort can be installed by running pip install isort
tests.purpose: Verify isort sorts imports alphabetically in a single specified file, confirming the core documented CLI workflow and that the pip-installed entrypoint runs successfully.

evidence: Running isort mypythonfile.py mypythonfile2.py from the command line sorts the imports in the specified files.
tests.purpose: Verify isort sorts imports independently across multiple files passed as separate arguments in a single invocation.
Verify isort . recursively sorts imports in all Python files under the current directory, including nested subdirectories.

evidence:
To view proposed changes without applying them:

isort mypythonfile.py --diff
tests.purpose: Verify isort --diff prints the proposed reordering to stdout without modifying the target file on disk.

evidence: isort can also be used to verify that code is correctly formatted by running it with -c. Any files that contain incorrectly sorted and/or formatted imports will be outputted to stderr.
tests.purpose: Realistic failure case: verify isort -c (check-only) reports an incorrectly sorted file as an error to stderr with a nonzero exit code, and leaves the file unmodified.

evidence: isort can also be used to verify that code is correctly formatted by running it with -c.
tests.purpose: Verify isort -c succeeds with exit code 0 and no error output when the file's imports are already correctly sorted, and leaves the file unmodified.
Verify the documented Python library API: importing isort and calling isort.file() sorts the imports of the target file on disk.
Verify the installed package's declared minimum Python version (from packaging metadata) matches the README's stated 3.10+ requirement.
